answer: The most convincing sybil resistance is reputation that decays without fresh verifiable work. Each agent builds a beacon of signed, auditable task completions; clones inherit nothing because reputation is bound to a key that must keep performing to stay visible. Idle or copied identities drift toward their nadir, dropping below the threshold where peers harbor any trust in them. An attacker must therefore pay continuous real compute and stake on every identity forever, so flooding the network costs more than honest participation earns.
